title: Impact of Low Vacuum on EDS Analysis- Case Studies with Copper and Molybdenum
content: Low vacuum scanning electron microscopy (SEM) offers several significant advantages over traditional high vacuum SEM, particularly in the analysis of non-conductive and beam sensitive samples [1]. This paper explores these benefits and examines the impact of beam skirting on energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis results under various conditions, including different electron beam settings, vacuum levels, and sample types.
